title: Channel
lead: Channels are the primary inter-coroutine communication mechanism.

sections.heading: Declaration
sections.after_text: Name a channel with `const`. `Channel<T>` is an audited synchronization handle: its binding is stable while `send`/`recv` mutate protected runtime state.

sections.heading: Timed operations
bullets: `sendTimeout(value, milliseconds)` returns SendResult; `recvTimeout(milliseconds)` returns Recv<T>. Closed results remain distinct from Timeout.
The duration is i64 in 0..86_400_000; out-of-range values raise NumericRange before the Channel operation. Zero performs one queue attempt.
A positive duration uses one monotonic deadline. The host supplies the clock; failed, zero or backward readings raise HostError rather than Timeout. Repeated waits never restart the deadline.
Evaluate receiver, message and duration once in source order, including Unit message side effects. Pending polls reuse those values; committed peer delivery wins over later withdrawal.
Both methods conservatively may suspend. Type admission and Sendable evidence remain separate from root permission and value Error effects.

sections.heading: Concurrency rules
bullets: The target Channel<T> payload domain requires copyable, storable, Sendable T; complete channel/go qualification remains separate from this contract
Qualified channel handles may be captured by go closures when the full type satisfies Sendable
Array payloads preserve logical copies without a required copy/move marker; class and synchronized identities are not duplicated or frozen
Noncopyable resources are outside the first Channel<T> payload domain; const or a synchronization wrapper cannot bypass Sendable checks
